rows.09:3444:
Mr. Sakurai stopped once more.
And sure enough, the other footsteps stopped too.
...There was no doubt about it.
The intruder was behind him.
Mr. Sakurai was certain of it.{p}Now, should he just whirl around and lunge at whoever it was...?
rows.09:3528: Turn around and lunge at them
rows.09:3540: Turn around and switch on the flashlight
rows.09:3560: Don't turn around; keep going and see what happens
rows.09:3598:
"Who's there?!"
The instant he turned, Mr. Sakurai aimed the flashlight where the intruder's face ought to be and switched it on.
The glare was so bright that Mr. Sakurai himself had to squint.
For a moment he was dazzled, but when he quickly strained his eyes... there was no one there.{p}
rows.09:37ac:
"...That's strange."
Mr. Sakurai tilted his head, then slowly stepped toward the spot his light was shining on.
rows.09:3834:
That was when it happened.
The other footsteps started up again.{p}
rows.09:389c: Startled, Mr. Sakurai stopped in his tracks.
rows.09:38cc:
And then the other footsteps stopped too.
When had they slipped around behind him?
Mr. Sakurai couldn't stop the hand gripping the flashlight from shaking violently.
rows.09:397c:
Even so, he had to find out.
If whoever it was really was behind him, he had to find out, no matter what.
Driven by that sense of duty, Mr. Sakurai gulped down the spit that had pooled in his mouth.{p}But it was also true that he was scared, scared out of his wits.
rows.09:3ae0: Mr. Sakurai turned around and swung the flashlight about wildly.{p}
rows.09:3b30:
...But the single thin beam of light showed him nothing at all.
"Where are you?!"{p}
rows.09:3ba4:
Mr. Sakurai stomped all over the floor, deliberately making his footsteps loud, and walked around with no aim at all.
And would you believe it, the footsteps followed right along with him.
Whenever Mr. Sakurai walked, he heard the footsteps.
What's more, the other footsteps matched his own exactly, coming at precisely the same loudness.
Always from behind him...
And whenever he stopped walking, the footsteps stopped dead too, as if they were reading Mr. Sakurai's mind.{p}
rows.09:3dfc:
"Hah... hah..."
At last Mr. Sakurai was worn out, his shoulders heaving with every breath.
His face was drenched with sweat.
Not so much from the muggy heat; it was cold sweat.
rows.09:3ebc:
...Squeak, squeak.{p}Mr. Sakurai focused every nerve on his ears.
Can you believe it?
The other footsteps were coming from behind him.
Even though he was standing still.
rows.09:3f5c: He couldn't hear his own footsteps, and yet now he could clearly hear the other footsteps, and only them.
rows.09:3fbc: And the distance that had stayed more or less the same kept closing, closer and closer.
rows.09:3ffc: As the gap closed, he felt as if a cold wind were blowing on him from behind.
rows.09:4044:
And at last the footsteps stopped dead, as if they had nestled right up against Mr. Sakurai's back.
The cold was like sticking his face into a freezer.
Something was definitely behind him.
Something that wasn't human...
Right now, he felt, he might be able to see it.
Should he turn around and look?
Or should he break into a run and escape?{p}He had only two choices left now.
rows.09:41b8:
As he whirled around, Mr. Sakurai pointed the flashlight.
And there...{p}
rows.09:4214:
"AAAAAAAAAAAAAGH!"
Mr. Sakurai's scream echoed through the school in the middle of the night.{p}
rows.09:4284:
...It was the next morning
when they found Mr. Sakurai, wandering aimlessly and unsteadily across the schoolyard.
With the flashlight still switched on, he was staggering round and round the schoolyard like a drunk.
Drool dribbled slackly from his mouth, his hair had turned pure white, and his face had aged as if he'd grown thirty years older all at once.
And,
"...It is my friend.
...And I am its friend.
...Let's all die together.
...Let's die and have fun."
he was singing, so they say, to an eerie little tune.{p}
rows.09:4460:
Mr. Sakurai was admitted to a hospital for treatment.
The treatment isn't making much progress, and I hear there's almost no hope of recovery.
And they say he still hums that song even now...
What on earth did Mr. Sakurai see?
Did he see something truly horrifying, I wonder?
And is that thing still lurking in the old school building, even now?
If the old school building gets torn down soon...
what on earth will become of it?
...My story ends here.
Thank you very much.{p}
rows.09:463c:
I see. Then you won't mind the story you're about to hear.
Good, good.
Then I can tell it without holding anything back.
It's about that old school building...{p}
rows.09:46d0:
I see.
This might actually be good.
You won't have any preconceptions, so it'll be worth telling you a scary story.
Old wooden buildings are, how should I put it, brittle, or musty, or dusty, aren't they?
That stale old smell lies there dozing, and when you rattle the door open, the air inside comes rushing out at you, doesn't it?
I hate that.
Doesn't it feel like a different world?
The old school building is like that too, I'd say.
Oh, no, I've never actually been inside it.
It's been many years since the old school building stopped being used, but the teachers did at least keep patrolling it.
And there's a story about one of those teachers' patrols...{p}
rows.09:491c:
Back then, there was a student teacher named Ms. Sasaki, I hear.
Student teachers usually go back to their old school to do their training, don't they?
Ms. Sasaki, too, had been coming to school in this very uniform only a few years before.
No one would ever make a student teacher do the night patrols of the school, right?
But that year, of all years, a spiteful teacher pushed to have her do it.{p}
rows.09:4a74:
Of course, she wasn't supposed to do it alone.
"Good luck tonight, Ms. Sasaki.
Ho ho ho."
"You make it sound so easy..."
No matter how old you get, your seniors are always mean.
That was what Ms. Sasaki thought.
"Just my luck. This year of all years, we have to patrol the old school building too. This is the worst."
Back in her student days, she'd been in the tennis club.
She found herself remembering the stories about the old school building that she'd heard at a ghost-story session during training camp.
"It's bringing back all kinds of memories...
Honestly, you seniors... I'm going to hold this against you."
That day there was supposed to be one more teacher on night duty, but there had been a death in that teacher's family, and they suddenly had to go home.
So Ms. Sasaki ended up doing the patrol all by herself.
"Well, if it's come to this, I might as well just brave it out.
Grumble, grumble..."
The old school building was three stories tall, and of course it had no electricity.
"Why do they keep this building around forever?
And up close, it looks even more dreadful."
Complaining all the while, Ms. Sasaki went inside.{p}
rows.09:4df0:
I think part of her wanted to see something scary, too.
The place was off-limits, so she must have been curious about it.
Ms. Sasaki was the nosy type, easily carried away by anything exciting.
She was still a college girl back then, after all.{p}
rows.09:4edc: She decided to go up to the third floor first, then work her way down floor by floor.
rows.09:4f2c: Relying on the feeble light of her flashlight, she climbed the stairs as they creaked, creak, creak, testing each step so she wouldn't miss her footing.{p}
rows.09:506c:
When she pointed the flashlight at a window, she saw her own faint reflection in the thin glass.
As she stared at it, she felt as though another shadow were overlapping her reflection, and she couldn't help jerking the flashlight away.{p}
rows.09:5130:
"I was acting tough, but I really do feel scared and alone..."
Then, done with the third floor, she went down to the second.{p}
rows.09:519c:
"The second floor is in much worse shape."
When she shone the light into the classrooms, she could see broken window glass and old nails sticking out all over the place.{p}
rows.09:5220:
As she made her way forward, crunching the thin scattered glass underfoot, crack, crack,
"Huh?"
rows.09:5278:
Her body wouldn't move forward.
"Hey, come on, you're joking, right?"
It felt like something had hold of her.
"Let go of me, let go, I said☆
Ugh, if you don't let go, you're getting this☆"{p}
rows.09:5330:
There was a ripping sound, something tearing.
"Huh..."
She had snagged herself on a protruding nail and had been struggling against it.
"How awful!
This blouse cost a fortune!
Argh, I'm so mad!"
It was her own fault for jumping to conclusions, but she conveniently ignored that and sulked, I'm told.{p}
rows.09:553c:
She hurried down the stairs, and was just about to head along the long first-floor corridor when...
"?"
She could hear something.
A child was laughing.
rows.09:55b0:
What's more, it sounded like a baby.
"Ahahaha, hee-hee-hee..."{p}
rows.09:5760:
Again, she hurriedly turned to face forward.
The laughter came closer and closer.
From behind her.
rows.09:583c:
"What do I do?
Why would there be a baby laughing in the old school building?
No, no, no, it's getting closer☆
What do I do?
Why★
This isn't fair!
Why is this happening?!☆"
She was in a total panic.
"Don't turn around, whatever you do☆"
Just as she murmured that, as if telling herself, the baby leapt and latched onto her back.{p}
